clue.text: Commonplace pedantries perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of pedantries might be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a string of pedantic remarks as rather ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging all ten letters of PEDANTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and ordinary, lacking any imagination.

clue.text: Bet you'll find one on the Cam!

definitions.text: you'll find one on the Cam!

explanation.surface: A wager about what boats a visitor will spot on Cambridge's river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river through Cambridge, where flat-bottomed boats poled along are a famous sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To punt is to gamble or place a wager; it is also the flat boat poled along the Cambridge river.

clue.text: Could it make a joiner spring into action?

indicators.note: into tells us the spring word is placed inside the action word

parts.note: action, something being done, is doing
a spring of water is a well

explanation.surface: Is there something that could get a carpenter leaping into action?
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container. The surface makes 'spring' a leap and 'joiner' a carpenter; here a joiner is anything that fastens timber together.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden pegs fitted into drilled holes are used to fasten two pieces of timber together in joinery.

clue.text: As from then

explanation.surface: A terse gloss on two words of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction can mean because, like 'as'; it also means from a past time until now.

clue.text: About to get togged up? That's correct

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to get togged up is to put on clothes, to dress

explanation.surface: Someone about to put on their smart clothes is told they have got it right.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right a wrong or an imbalance is to remedy or rectify it.

clue.text: Insult a Catholic priest in spring

indicators.note: in places the priest's abbreviation within the word for a spring

parts.note: a font is a spring or fountain (also a source)
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a title for a Catholic priest

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest is offended while out in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' reads as the season but is FONT, a fountain or source.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate slight or offensive act is an outrage to someone's dignity.

clue.text: Fail to make little Florence quiet

parts.note: Flo is a short form of the name Florence
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A failure to get young Florence to hush.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or venture that flops is unsuccessful, falling flat.

clue.text: Weapon enabling the French to capture African nationalists

indicators.note: to capture means the French article holds the nationalists inside it

parts.note: le is French for the
the ANC is the African National Congress

explanation.surface: French arms allowing the capture of an African independence movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is an armament.

clue.text: Its present form has attractive features

indicators.note: present form suggests these letters take on a new shape when rearranged

explanation.surface: A gift whose current shape is pleasing to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' signals rearranging the letters of ITS PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Good looks and charm in a person or object amount to its loveliness.

clue.text: Continues to make gains

explanation.surface: Business keeps going and turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means goes on or carries on; as a plural noun it means money taken from a sale or event.

clue.text: Currently batting, but without hope of success

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease in a hopeless position.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the first is 'now in', describing a batter currently at the crease in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter who has gone out to bat is 'now in'; a no-win situation offers no chance of victory.

clue.text: In resisting attack army corps gains respect

indicators.note: In tells us the army corps sits inside the word for resisting attack

parts.note: resisting attack is defence
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

explanation.surface: An army unit under assault holds firm and earns esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite submission and esteem shown to someone is regard or courtesy.

clue.text: Achates has to change his self-image

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
the ego is one's sense of self

explanation.surface: A mythical hero must revise how he sees himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Achates is the loyal companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid, proverbial for faithful friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates, the hero's devoted friend, stands for a second self or inseparable companion.

clue.text: Cold and warmth are deceptive

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A remark that hot and cold sensations can fool you.
explanation.definitionFit: To act dishonestly to gain an advantage is to deceive; 'they are deceptive' is 'they swindle'.

clue.text: Jointly got a labourer under control

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
a matter in hand is being dealt with, under control

explanation.surface: Someone managed to bring a worker into line together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something together, closely connected, is like holding each other's palms.

clue.text: Burning sulphur settles

parts.note: something burning is alight
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Burning sulphur sinks down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that comes to rest on a perch lands, or settles, there.

clue.text: Stolen silverware used by a restaurateur

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
plate is household silver or gold ware

explanation.surface: Stolen silver cutlery ends up in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated cooking surface is equipment a restaurant kitchen would rely on.

clue.text: Restrict one press chief in London

indicators.note: in puts the one and the editor within the word for London

parts.note: Londoners call the capital simply 'town'
I is the Roman numeral one
ed is short for editor, a newspaper's chief

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss in the capital imposes limits.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone or hold them fast is to tether or bind them.

clue.text: Exaggerate a dictator's position

explanation.surface: An overblown claim about where a tyrant stands.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'over state', the second reading is a dictator's place above the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstress or inflate a claim is to overdo it; a despot rules over the nation.

clue.text: What Jack once followed follows Jack

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
Jack Tar is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a sailor used to track.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors once navigated by the stars; Sirius, the brightest, is the one named here.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafarers steered by bright heavenly bodies such as Sirius before modern instruments.

clue.text: Avoid being a burden

explanation.surface: Steer clear of becoming a load on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' here is the old word for the chorus of a song, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abstain; as a noun it is a recurring chorus, which 'burden' also means.

clue.text: Nazi deputy embraced East German entertainer

indicators.note: embraced means the deputy's name wraps around the German word

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was deputy to Hitler
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: Hitler's deputy hugged someone from the GDR.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who receives and entertains guests is a party giver.

clue.text: Henry and Rachel settled in Wales

definitions.note: a place in Wales, the town with its famous castle

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: settled suggests the letters of Rachel come to rest in a new order

explanation.surface: A couple named Henry and Rachel set up home in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This coastal town in Gwynedd is known for its medieval castle.

clue.text: Plane crash in southern Asia

definitions.note: a Himalayan country of southern Asia

indicators.note: crash suggests the letters of plane are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft comes down somewhere in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked Himalayan kingdom lies in the south of the continent.

clue.text: Shot warm-hearted RAF officer

indicators.note: hearted says the warm word forms the heart of the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: PO is Pilot Officer in the RAF
hot is very warm

explanation.surface: A kindly air force officer was shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture taken with a camera is a snap.

clue.text: Leading medic is not out of the wood

indicators.note: is not out of means the medic stays within the wood

parts.note: a forest is a large wood
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: The chief doctor has not yet escaped danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out of the wood' looks like the idiom for still in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being first in rank or position is to be at the front.

clue.text: One of little vision admits 'is aspiration

definitions.text: One of little vision admits 'is aspiration

parts.words: One of little vision admits 'is aspiration
parts.note: the short-sighted speaker, dropping the aspirate as the apostrophe in 'is shows, would say 'my hope' without its H

explanation.surface: A short-sighted man owns up to what he hopes for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' means both a hope and the sound H, which the Cockney speaker drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-sighted person sees distant things poorly.

clue.text: Predisposition to be dishonest

explanation.surface: A tendency toward crooked dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural inclination is a leaning; 'bent' is also slang for corrupt.

clue.text: Total change of opinion regarding impudence

parts.note: about means regarding
face means cheek or effrontery

explanation.surface: A complete reversal of views about someone's cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of position or attitude is a U-turn.

clue.text: Old, wise and brave

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: Praise for someone elderly, sensible and courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' is a noun here: a Native American warrior; the Osage are a people of the US Great Plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior of a North American Indian people is traditionally called a brave.

clue.text: Returning ill-humour spells disaster

indicators.note: Returning tells us the word for ill-humour is read backwards

parts.note: a mood is a fit of bad temper

explanation.surface: A recurring bad temper brings catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin or a terrible fate is calamity.

clue.text: Competing, as it happened

explanation.surface: Taking part, as things turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant in a contest is taking part in it; the phrase also means 'as things turned out'.
